deed: Israeli company Soos saves male chicks from culling in the egg industry
title: Israeli company Soos plays sounds to eggs so that male chicks hatch as females and are not culled

trailer.text: According to Poultry World, the global egg industry raises 15 billion chicks every year, and culls the half that are male.
Haj Mohammad, from an Arab-Muslim village in northern Israel, raises chickens in his yard, and according to Alter he noticed that under certain conditions more females hatched there.
According to the company, the system Soos developed turns male embryos inside the egg into egg-laying females, using sound waves and vibration and without chemicals.
In November 2020, Soos won a prize of a million dollars in the Grow-NY competition, and the technology was tested in pilots on farms in Europe and the US.

glance.label: Where
glance.value: According to NoCamels, Beersheva, in southern Israel.

glance.label: How
glance.value: Sound waves and vibration during incubation

paragraphs.text: According to Yael Alter, the egg industry culls 7.5 billion day-old male chicks every year, because they do not lay eggs and are not used for meat.
According to AgFunderNews, raising the males of laying breeds for meat is not economically viable.
According to ISRAEL21c, they are killed by gassing, suffocation, electrocution or shredding while still alive.
According to Alter, the culling costs money needlessly and wastes incubation space, electricity and water.
She says it also causes the animals significant suffering and abuse.

stations.title: The world begins to ban it

paragraphs.text: According to AFP, animal rights activists called the culling of chicks "barbaric".
In June 2016 the trade group United Egg Producers, which represents much of the American egg industry, announced a plan to stop killing male chicks by 2020.
According to The Investor, Germany pledged in 2015 to end the culling, Switzerland pledged in 2019, and France in 2020.
According to AFP, the German ban came into effect in 2022.
That same year, French farmers were given until the end of the year to comply with new restrictions.
According to Syracuse University, in 2023 Italy, Austria and Luxembourg were also in the process of banning it.
According to ISRAEL21c, that same year three Israeli startups were working on different ways to stop the culling.

stations.title: A coop next to a utility pole

paragraphs.text: Nashat Haj Mohammad comes from Kaukab Abu al-Hija, an Arab-Muslim village in northern Israel.
According to NoCamels, he manages a blood laboratory at an Israeli hospital and raises chickens in his yard as a hobby.
According to NoCamels, when he moved the coop next to a utility pole, he saw that more female chicks than male chicks were hatching.

According to NoCamels, he experimented for five years: he moved the coop from place to place and played sounds at different volumes and at different times, to find out which conditions produce more females.
According to Alter, Nashat met her at an industry event.
She was then the CEO of an international company that built poultry facilities.
According to ISRAEL21c, the two founded Soos in 2017 with money from Takwin, a fund that supports Arab-Jewish Israeli startups.
According to Alter, the company was founded after a first raise of 400 thousand dollars from Takwin Labs.

stations.title: A tray that plays sound to eggs

paragraphs.text: According to NoCamels, the sex of the embryo in a chicken egg is not determined until the sixth day of three weeks of incubation.
According to NoCamels, Soos uses this window and introduces sound vibration into incubation, which increases the chance that males too will develop ovaries.
According to NoCamels, the eggs lie in trays with speakers that make them vibrate.
According to NoCamels, each “smart tray” has motion sensors that measure how much vibration the eggs sense.
According to Alter, the protocol is patented, and it controls humidity, temperature, CO2 level, and the frequency and intensity of the sound.
According to ISRAEL21c, the sound waves cause embryos that are genetically male to develop ovaries, and after 21 days they hatch as females that can lay eggs.
According to NoCamels, the hens remain genetically male, but they are female in body.
According to Soos, the treatment is safe for the embryos, does not penetrate the egg, and involves no genetic modification or hormones.
According to NoCamels, even Soos researchers are not sure why it works.
Van Trump Report also wrote in 2024 that scientists do not understand why the method works.
According to Alter, other methods test the sex of the egg, take seconds per egg, can harm incubation, and usually work only after the seventh day.
According to NoCamels, the common method drills a hole in the shell and extracts fluid, and this sometimes causes infection and the death of the embryo.
Alon Gozlan of Soos said that most competitors detect what is inside the egg, and that no one is doing sex reversal to increase productivity.
According to ISRAEL21c, Soos's spinoff company, Ovo Technology, is doing the opposite for the broiler industry.

stations.title: From the lab to the farm in Auburn

paragraphs.text: According to Alter, in laboratory incubators of 70 eggs 80% females hatched, and in industrial incubators of 4,800 eggs 60% hatched.
She says the difficulty is transmitting a uniform sound wave, so that every egg hears the same sound, and this is the company's biggest challenge.
As part of the Grow-NY grant, Soos was required to work with a farm and a university in New York.
It chose a commercial farm in Auburn, about half an hour west of Syracuse, and researchers James Crill and Steve Dorus of Syracuse University.
According to the university, Soos staff installed incubators with sound devices there in early 2022.
Crill said the researchers want to understand how the sound waves cause the female genes to act instead of the male ones.
Efrat Petel, Soos's US manager, said that in Experiment 26, 69% females hatched in one set and 63% in another set.
According to Syracuse University, if the work succeeds, it could lead to a new incubation method that would save billions of dollars and billions of chicks a year.
According to NoCamels, the technology has already been used on an egg farm in Upstate New York, where 1,200 “reverse chicks” hatched.
According to NoCamels, it was also used on one of the largest egg farms in Israel, where 200 hatched.
According to NoCamels, Soos is leading two pilots: one with Italy's Amadori and one with Belgium's largest egg producer.
According to Alter, the Food Tech Accelerator in Italy connected the company with one of the country's largest integrators, for its first international pilot.
According to Alter, Soos sells to businesses: the system's end users are commercial hatcheries, and the customers are integrators in the poultry industry.
Alter told The Investor that converting an existing incubator costs $3,000 to $10,000.
According to the company, an incubator that costs 25 to 30 thousand dollars pays back the investment in less than three years.
According to The Investor, the company planned to enter Switzerland, France, the US and Australia, and later South Korea and other Asian countries.
According to NoCamels, in 2022 it wanted to raise $20 million within two years and expand into hatcheries in the US and Europe.
According to NoCamels, worldwide the method could save up to six billion male chicks.

stations.title: A million dollars and the people behind it

paragraphs.text: According to Israel Hayom, more than 260 applicants entered the Grow-NY competition in 2020, and the 20 finalists presented remotely because of COVID.
In November 2020 Soos won the competition's grand prize, one million dollars.
Alter said that with this money the company plans to build a poultry research hub in New York, and to create more than twenty research and engineering jobs there within two years.
According to Alter, after the win Soos had 10 employees, and it had raised $3.2 million, including the prize.
According to The Investor, Soos was in the 2020 cohort of SparkLabs Cultiv8, an agri-tech accelerator from Australia.
According to Alter, the company's largest investors are Israeli venture capital funds, which gave it the connections it needed to get started.
According to ISRAEL21c, Yael Alter is the CEO, and Dr. Shlomit Fedida-Metula is the chief scientist.
In 2023, Efrat Petel managed Soos in the US.
In 2023, Alon Gozlan was vice president of business development.

stations.title: An industry that is hard to change

paragraphs.text: Alter said the farmers are very conservative and see no reason to change something that works.
Gozlan said commercial hatcheries are very traditional when they buy, and Soos is asking them to replace a core technology and the equipment.
According to Alter, it is hard to find industry players or investors willing to fund long research before there is a finished product.
According to Alter, in the large incubators the result dropped, because it is hard to make sure every egg hears the same sound.
According to ISRAEL21c, in July 2023 Gozlan said the technology was still about a year away from the market.

claims.quote: Soos was founded in 2017 by Nashaat Haj-Mohammed and Yael Alter with funding from Takwin, a VC supporting Arab-Jewish Israeli startups.

claims.text: לפי NoCamels (2022), סוס היא סטארט-אפ בבאר שבע שבדרום ישראל, החלוץ בתהליך היפוך מין שהופך עוברי אפרוחים בתוך הביצה מזכר לנקבה.
claims.quote: Soos, a startup in Beersheva, southern Israel, is pioneering a sex-reversal process that literally turns chick embryos inside the egg from male to female

claims.text: לפי Poultry World, תעשיית הביצים העולמית מייצרת מדי שנה 15 מיליארד אפרוחים; מחציתם נקבות והמחצית השנייה, 7.5 מיליארד זכרים, מושמדת.
claims.quote: Every year, the global egg industry produces 15 billion chicks. Half of them are female and grow up to be functional layers, but the other 7.5 billion are males and are culled

claims.text: לפי NoCamels, נשאת חאג' מוחמד, מייסד-שותף של סוס, גילה את התופעה בכפר מולדתו כוכב אבו אל-היג'א, כפר ערבי-מוסלמי בצפון ישראל.
claims.quote: Nashat Haj Mohammad, Co-founder of Soos, discovered the phenomenon himself in his hometown of Kaukab Abu al-Hika, an Arab-Muslim village in the north of Israel.

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, לחאג' מוחמד יש תרנגולות מטילות בחצר, והוא הבחין שבתנאים מסוימים בקעו יותר נקבות מזכרים.

claims.quote: It essentially transforms male chicken embryos into egg-laying females in ovo using non-invasive and chemical-free sound waves and vibration, according to the startup.

claims.text: בנובמבר 2020 הוכרזה סוס כזוכת הפרס הגדול בסך מיליון דולר בסיבוב השני של תחרות Grow-NY העולמית לעסקי מזון וחקלאות.

claims.text: סוס יצרה שיתוף פעולה עם חווה מסחרית באובורן, ניו יורק, כ-30 דקות ממערב לסירקיוז, ועם החוקרים קריל ודורוס.
claims.quote: They formed a collaboration with a commercial farm located in Auburn, New York, around 30 minutes west of Syracuse, and Crill and Dorus.

claims.text: ג'יימס קריל וסטיב דורוס, חוקרים באוניברסיטת סירקיוז, משתפים פעולה עם סוס בפרויקט.
claims.quote: James Crill, professor of practice in the Forensic Science Institute, and Steve Dorus, professor in the Department of Biology, are collaborating on the project

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת סירקיוז, נציגי סוס התקינו ואיטבו את הדוגרים עם מכשירי הקול בחווה באובורן, ניו יורק, בתחילת 2022.
claims.quote: Their initial work involved installing and optimizing the incubators at the farm with the sound wave devices in early 2022.

claims.text: קריל אמר שהחוקרים מבקשים לקבוע כיצד גלי הקול גורמים לביטוי גנים נקביים על פני גנים זכריים.
claims.quote: We are looking to determine how the sound waves are triggering certain female genes to be expressed over the male genes.

claims.text: אפרת פטל, מנהלת סוס ארה"ב, אמרה שבניסוי 26 נמצא יחס של 69% נקבות בסט אחד ו-63% בסט אחר.
claims.quote: On Experiment 26, we found a 69% female ratio in one set and a 63% female ratio in another set.

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת סירקיוז, העבודה עשויה להוביל לשיטת דגירה חדשה שתחולל מהפכה בענף העופות ותחסוך מיליארדי דולרים ומיליארדי אפרוחים בשנה.
claims.quote: Their work could result in a new method of incubation that would revolutionize the poultry industry and save both billions of dollars and billions of chicks each year.

claims.text: לפי NoCamels, סוס מובילה שני פיילוטים של מו"פ, אחד עם Amadori האיטלקית והשני עם יצרנית הביצים הגדולה בבלגיה.
claims.quote: Soos is also leading two R&D pilots, one with Amadori, one of the leading companies in Italy’s agro-food sector, and the other with the biggest producer of eggs in Belgium.

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, מאיץ Food Tech Accelerator באיטליה קישר את סוס לאחד האינטגרטורים הגדולים באיטליה להתחלת הפיילוט הבינלאומי הראשון.
claims.quote: Food Tech Accelerator in Italy connected us with one of Italy’s largest poultry integrators to start our first international pilot.

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, סוס היא חברת B2B; משתמשי הקצה הם מדגרות מסחריות והלקוחות הם אינטגרטורים בענף העופות.
claims.quote: We are a B2B company. Our solution’s end-users are commercial hatcheries, while our customers are poultry integrators.

claims.text: אלטר אמרה ל-The Investor שהמרת דוגרים קיימים עולה 3,000 עד 10,000 דולר, ולכן אימוץ הטכנולוגיה כמעט מובן מאליו עבור החקלאי.
claims.quote: If converting the existing incubators, it costs between $3,000 to US$10,000, then it is almost a no-brainer to adopt the incubator to improvise farmer’s yields

claims.text: לפי החברה, כפי שדווח ב-The Investor ב-2020, ההשקעה בדוגר שעלותו 25-30 אלף דולר תוחזר בפחות מ-3 שנים.
claims.quote: the company says that the investments on an incubator that currently costs $25,000 to $30,000 would be covered in less than 3 years

claims.text: לפי The Investor (נובמבר 2020), החברה הישראלית תכננה להיכנס בשנה שלאחר מכן לשווייץ, צרפת, ארה"ב ואוסטרליה, ובהמשך לדרום קוריאה ולמדינות אסיה נוספות.
claims.quote: The Israeli company aims to make a foray into Switzerland, France, the US and Australia next year, and South Korea and other Asian countries later.

claims.text: לפי NoCamels (2022), החברה רצתה לגייס 20 מיליון דולר בשנתיים הקרובות ולהתמקד בהתרחבות למדגרות בארה"ב ובאירופה.
claims.quote: Within the next two years, the company wants to raise $20 million, and focus on expanding into hatcheries across the US and Europe.

claims.text: לפי NoCamels, בכל העולם השיטה עשויה להציל עד שישה מיליארד אפרוחים זכרים.
claims.quote: Across the poultry world, that could translate into saving up to six billion male chicks.

claims.text: לפי ישראל היום, מעל 260 מועמדים נכנסו לתחרות Grow-NY ב-2020, ו-20 הגמרים הציגו וירטואלית בגלל מגפת הקורונה.
claims.quote: Over 260 applicants entered this year's Grow-NY competition. The top 20 finalists submitted their pitches virtually, due to the COVID pandemic.

claims.text: אלטר אמרה שבכסף הפרס סוס מתכננת ליצור בשנתיים הקרובות יותר מעשרים משרות מחקר והנדסה בשכר גבוה, באמצעות הקמת מרכז מחקר לעופות בניו יורק.
claims.quote: With our Grow-NY prize money, we plan to create over twenty high-paying research and engineering jobs in the next two years, by building the NY Poultry Research Hub

claims.text: לאחר הזכייה תכננה סוס להרחיב גיוס עובדים ולהקים מרכז מחקר לעופות בניו יורק.
claims.quote: With its new cash infusion, Soos plans to ramp up hiring and build a poultry research hub in New York

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, בעת הראיון (לאחר זכיית 2020) לסוס 10 עובדים במשרה מלאה, היא גייסה 3.2 מיליון דולר כולל מיליון הדולר מ-Grow-NY, והייתה בשלב פיילוט לפני מסחור.
claims.quote: Today Soos has 10 full-time employees, has raised $3.2 million in capital — including the $1 million won in the 2020 Grow-NY competition — and is currently in the pilot stage prior to commercialization.

claims.text: לפי The Investor, סוס הייתה חלק ממחזור 2020 של SparkLabs Cultiv8, מאיץ אגרו-טק מבוסס אוסטרליה.
claims.quote: Soos is a part of the 2020 cohort of SparkLabs Cultiv8, which is an Australia-based agri-tech accelerator program that’s a part of SparkLabs Group.

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, המשקיעים הגדולים של סוס הם קרנות הון סיכון ישראליות שסיפקו את הקשרים הדרושים להקמת החברה.
claims.quote: Our largest investors are Israeli VCs who provided us with the connections needed to start the company.

claims.text: ISRAEL21c מציין את ד"ר שלומית פדידה-מטולה כמדענית הראשית של סוס ואת יעל אלטר כמנכ"לית.
claims.quote: Soos Chief Scientist Dr. Shlomit Fedida-Metula and CEO Yael Alter, with (female) baby chicks.

claims.text: אלון גוזלן, סגן נשיא פיתוח עסקי בסוס, אמר שענף המדגרות המסחריות מסורתי מאוד בהתנהגות הרכישה ושסוס מבקשת מהן להחליף טכנולוגיית ליבה ואת הציוד.
claims.quote: The commercial hatchery industry is very traditional in its buying behavior and we are asking them to replace their core technology with a different form of incubation using different equipment.

claims.text: אלטר אמרה שהחקלאים שמרנים מאוד ואינם רואים סיבה לשנות דבר שעובד.
claims.quote: The farmers are very conservative – if something works, it works, and they see no reason to change that

claims.text: לדברי אלטר, קשה למצוא גורמים בענף או משקיעים המוכנים להשקיע בשלבי מו"פ ארוכי טווח לפני קיום מוצר סופי.
claims.quote: It is very difficult to find industry players or investors who are willing to invest in long-term R&D phases before the final product.

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c (יולי 2023), גוזלן אמר שהטכנולוגיה רחוקה כשנה מהשוק.
claims.quote: Gozlan says the technology is about a year away from the market.

claims.text: לפי The Spoon, כ-6 מיליארד אפרוחים זכרים מושמדים מדי שנה.
claims.quote: This means that 6 billion male chicks are culled each year

claims.text: סוס טוענת שבשינוי תדרי הקול, העוצמות, הלחות והטמפרטורה בדגירה היא יכולה להעלות את הסיכוי לבקיעת נקבה מ-50% לכמעט 80%.
claims.quote: Soos Technology claims they can increase the odds of hatching a female chick from 50% to near 80%.

claims.text: לפי The Investor (נובמבר 2020), אלטר אמרה שהטכנולוגיה מעלה את שיעור הנקבות בכ-5 עד 15 נקודות אחוז.
claims.quote: According to Yael Alter, Soos’ co-founder and CEO, the biotech startup’s technology enhances the ratio of female eggs by about 5 to 15 percentage points.

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת סירקיוז (2023), נתונים מוקדמים הראו שכ-61% מהאפרוחים שבקעו לאחר טיפול סוס היו נקבות.
claims.quote: Their early data shows promise, as around 61% of the hatched chicks who have undergone the Soos treatment have been female.

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c (2023), ביצים במגש החכם של סוס נחשפות לרעידות אקוסטיות ספציפיות במהלך ששת הימים הראשונים להתפתחות העוברית.
claims.quote: Eggs incubated in Soos Technology’s Smart Tray are exposed to specific acoustic vibrations during the first six days of embryonic development.

claims.text: פטל אמרה שחשיפה לשידורי קול בתדרים ובעוצמות מסוימים משפיעה משמעותית על תהליך שינוי המין, בעיקר כשהיא מבוצעת מיום 0 עד יום 16.
claims.quote: exposure to sound transmissions at certain frequencies and intensities in the hatchery significantly affects the sex change process, especially when it is performed from day 0 to day 16

claims.text: לפי The Investor מנובמבר 2020, החברה, שתוארה כבת ארבע שנים, גייסה עד אז 2.2 מיליון דולר משלושה משקיעים וביניהם SparkLabs, ותכננה לגייס 5 מיליון דולר בסבב A עד סוף השנה.
claims.quote: The four-year company has so far raised $2.2 million from three investors including SparkLabs and plans to raise $5 million by the end of the year in Series A funding.

claims.text: בנובמבר 2020 זכתה סוס בפרס של מיליון דולר בתחרות Grow-NY, והטכנולוגיה נוסתה בפיילוטים בחוות באירופה ובארה"ב.
